filesChanged.note: The two orchestrators were deliberately left unwired to the new async ambiguity-resolution stage in this pass - runStructureStage()/parseDocumentStructure() remain 100% synchronous and behavior-identical, per the backward-compatibility decision in 02-structural-triage-design.json. parseDocumentStructureWithTriage()/resolveStructuralAmbiguity() are complete, independently tested, and ready to be wired into either orchestrator as a follow-up (call parseDocumentStructureWithTriage instead of parseDocumentStructure, then await resolveStructuralAmbiguity for any ambiguousCandidates using the package's own companyId/instrumentKey/documentId as cache identity) - this was not done in this pass to avoid touching orchestrator.ts/analysis/orchestrator.ts, which are outside this workstream's minimal-diff mandate and carry their own extensive resumability/caching machinery.

architectureSummary: HIGH-CONFIDENCE DETERMINISTIC + BOUNDED SEMANTIC/STRUCTURAL CLASSIFICATION FOR AMBIGUITY + FAIL-CLOSED UNRESOLVED STATE, exactly as mandated. A new triage decision procedure (evaluateStructuralCandidateTriage, stage-structure.ts) classifies every raw regex candidate as CONFIDENT_HEADING / CONFIDENT_PROSE_REFERENCE / AMBIGUOUS using several independent, disclosed, purely-typographic signals (seam validation, continuation shape, paragraph break, ARTICLE adjacency, document start) - no single signal is universally decisive except the two directly, empirically validated ones (seam validity and ordinary-lowercase-continuation). AMBIGUOUS candidates are, by default, fail-closed excluded (parseDocumentStructureWithTriage) and only resolved by a new bounded classifier (structural-ambiguity-classifier.ts) when a caller explicitly runs resolveStructuralAmbiguity (structural-ambiguity-resolution.ts) - architecturally modeled on condition-suspicion-classifier.ts (StageCaller abstraction, tenant-scoped cache, three-valued verdict, synthetic-fallback fail-safe), independently at the type level (own wire schema, own cache, zero shared imports beyond generic infrastructure). The existing deterministic parseDocumentStructure()/runStructureStage() are completely UNCHANGED (a pure, behavior-preserving refactor extracted their span/rank-stack construction for reuse) - zero regression risk to the 59 pre-existing test files and the entire prior remediation history.
keyDesignChoices: Seam validation (VALIDATED_TERMINATED/ABSORBED_SENTENCE/INCOMPLETE_NO_TERMINAL) replaces the removed wrap-tolerance mechanism outright rather than repairing it - the auditor's own Case C/D minimal pair proved any hop-forward-and-guess design is unsound in general; an unresolved seam is now honestly AMBIGUOUS, never guessed.

A narrow, disclosed LOWERCASE_DEFINITIONAL exception ('means'/'shall mean') prevents the one universal lowercase-reject rule from over-firing on the real 'Term. means ...' definitions convention, without turning it into an open phrase list - exactly two fixed continuations recognized, both closed, near-universal legal-drafting tells.

IMMEDIATE_KEYWORD adjacency is bounded to <=1 newline of separation (not merely a small character count, which a 2-character '\n\n' paragraph break would satisfy just as well as true adjacency) - closes the auditor's own Part 3 final falsification (an unrelated, later real heading laundering a fully-absorbed fake candidate through an unbounded keyword lookahead).

Title-length plausibility (MAX_PLAUSIBLE_TITLE_LENGTH=110, mirroring SECTION_PATTERNS[0]'s own 90-char shape-based bound) prevents a crude, unbounded fallback pattern's own greedy title capture from being mistaken for a validated seam merely because it happens to end in one terminal period with nothing internal.
The triage system is purely ADDITIVE - parseDocumentStructure/runStructureStage are byte-identical to before this change, proven by a full pre/post regression run (2216+ tests unaffected).

coverage: title followed by digit-led body -> CONFIDENT_HEADING
title followed by quoted/defined-term body -> CONFIDENT_HEADING
wrapped title -> AMBIGUOUS (genuinely unresolvable seam; correct per spec, never a false reject)
ARTICLE immediately followed by SECTION -> CONFIDENT_HEADING (both nodes)
definitions-style 'Term. means ...' with strong (paragraph-break) evidence -> CONFIDENT_HEADING (deterministically FIXED, was a false negative under the old design)
definitions-style 'Term. means ...' with weak evidence -> AMBIGUOUS, correctly resolved LIKELY_HEADING by the classifier
complete citation sentence followed by a capitalized sentence -> AMBIGUOUS
citation followed by a quote-led sentence -> AMBIGUOUS
citation followed by an acronym-led sentence -> AMBIGUOUS
citation followed by a number-led sentence -> AMBIGUOUS
two unrelated short lines made heading-shaped by extraction -> AMBIGUOUS
real next heading shortly after a fake citation -> AMBIGUOUS (never CONFIDENT_HEADING; the real 3.10 heading is unaffected)

workstreamOPEN1WiringFix.note: NEW SECTION added by a follow-up workstream. Everything above this key is the ORIGINAL OPEN-1 record, unmodified. This section documents closing the exact gap the original record's own `filesChanged.note` (above) flagged and deliberately deferred: 'The two orchestrators were deliberately left unwired to the new async ambiguity-resolution stage in this pass.' `lib/contract-model/compiler/orchestrator.ts` (the legacy, quarantined Phase C compiler - see that file's own QUARANTINE NOTICE) is now wired. `lib/contract-model/analysis/orchestrator.ts` (runContractAnalysis) - the codebase's own explicitly-documented 'ONE authoritative live contract-analysis orchestration boundary', the actual entry point app/[companyId]/onboarding/documents/actions.ts calls - was NOT wired in this pass; see criticalCaveatAboutRealProductionImpact below.

whatWasWired.newFunction: runStructureStageWithAmbiguityResolution(documents, identity: {companyId, instrumentKey}, caller, cache?) - added to lib/contract-model/compiler/structural-ambiguity-resolution.ts (kept out of stage-structure.ts deliberately, preserving that file's own 'pure, deterministic, no LLM call' module-boundary discipline). Per document: calls parseDocumentStructureWithTriage; if a document has zero AMBIGUOUS candidates it costs zero classifier calls and its triage.nodes are used directly; otherwise resolveStructuralAmbiguity is called with a per-document StructuralAmbiguityCacheIdentity ({companyId, instrumentKey, sourceDocumentId: doc.documentId}). Confident nodes + resolved-ambiguous nodes are merged into the same StructuralNode[] shape/order runStructureStage always produced. Returns {status, output, notes, reviewSignals, metrics} - reviewSignals (StructuralReviewSignal[]) and metrics (StructuralAmbiguityResolutionRateMetrics) are the audit-trail fields the original design flagged as needing a real sink; they are threaded all the way to CompilerRunSummary.structuralReviewSignals/structuralAmbiguityMetrics (new fields), the closest existing pattern this file's own StageRunResult.notes convention offered (that field turned out to be dead code everywhere else in orchestrator.ts - never persisted by getOrRunStage, never read by any stages.push call - so this is a genuine new sink, not a reuse of a working prior pattern).
whatWasWired.instrumentKeyChoice: orchestrator.ts's CompilerPackageInput has no 'instrument' concept distinct from the package itself (that grouping is a Phase 2 substrate concept - package-graph/pipeline.ts) - the wiring passes packageKey as instrumentKey, matching classifyStructuralAmbiguity's own tenant-scoping requirement (a stable, unique-enough scope string, never a specific domain meaning).
whatWasWired.callSiteChange: orchestrator.ts's STRUCTURE stage closure changed from `const r = runStructureStage(documents); return {...r};` to `const r = await runStructureStageWithAmbiguityResolution(documents, {companyId, instrumentKey: packageKey}, caller); structuralReviewSignals = r.reviewSignals; structuralAmbiguityMetrics = r.metrics; return {status: r.status, output: r.output, notes: r.notes};` - `caller` (the real getStageCaller() already constructed a few lines above for every other LLM-calling stage) is passed straight through, never a new caller-acquisition mechanism.

cacheInvalidationDecision.reasoning: STRUCTURE is no longer purely deterministic - the same document text can now produce a genuinely different node set depending on the classifier's verdict on AMBIGUOUS candidates (an old-code case that had no third path at all). This is exactly the 'structural-parsing ALGORITHM change over unchanged document text' STRUCTURAL_INDEX_VERSION's own doc comment requires a bump for.
cacheInvalidationDecision.providerIdentityAlsoFoldedIntoStructureI: Yes - structureInputHash changed from hashParts([STRUCTURAL_INDEX_VERSION, ...documents]) to hashParts([STRUCTURAL_INDEX_VERSION, providerIdentity, ...documents]) (providerIdentity's own computation was moved earlier in the function, before the STRUCTURE stage, to make it available). Reasoning: STRUCTURE now depends on provider/model exactly like every other LLM-calling stage's own inputHash already accounts for - a credential becoming available where none existed before (synthetic -> real caller) must never be silently resumed as if nothing changed.
